newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say advancing into Kisangani city.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say advancing into Kisangani city.

text.p: Zaire rebels battling for the country's third largest city of Kisangani said on Saturday their forces were advancing into the city itself after capturing the international airport.
"The international airport has been taken and fighting is continuing in town," Raphael Ngenda told reporters at rebel headquarters in the eastern town of Goma.

The fall of Kisangani would be the biggest setback for the government since the rebels took up arms in October, vowing to topple veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko. They already hold towns and a large swathe of territory in the east.
In the Zambian capital Lusaka, military sources said Zairean soldiers had abandoned the town of Pweto in mineral-rich Shaba province which shares a lake border with northern Zambia.

"Our forces have detected the Zairean army fleeing Pweto and our intelligence so far confirms that all government troops have fled the town without a fight," a senior military official told Reuters in Nairobi by telephone from Lusaka.

If confirmed, the flight of the Zaireans from Pweto puts the rebels within 400 km (250 miles) reach of Lubumbashi, the capital of Shaba. A regional military source earlier told Reuters that the rebels were advancing on Pweto.

The rebels' Voice of the People broadcast from Goma also said the Zairean army (FAZ) was fleeing the city. Zairean rebels have seized control of around one-fifth of the country since the start of their campaign last October.
